notes.author: Chloe Nakamura
notes.text: Kickoff with Rosalind Achebe. Supporting procurement of an account-based fare system. $950k advisory engagement.

notes.author: Tariq Hassan
notes.text: Award recommended. Losing bidder filed a formal bid protest within 48 hours alleging inconsistent scoring between evaluators.

notes.author: Tariq Hassan
notes.text: Protest review found two evaluators' score sheets lacked written justification. Contract frozen for 5 months. Victor Lam: "Our paperwork was the weak point, not our decision."

notes.author: Chloe Nakamura
notes.text: Protest dismissed after re-scoring with contemporaneous written rationale. Award stands. Unusual situation; first protest in the agency's history.

simulation.note: Unusual single-engagement pattern: passes the leak check but is held back until a second unrelated engagement shows the same pattern.
simulation.lesson: In competitive public procurements, require every evaluator to record a short written justification for each score at the time of scoring. Consensus decisions without contemporaneous rationale are the most common point of failure when a losing bidder challenges an award, and can freeze a contract for months even when the underlying decision was sound.
simulation.why: Bid challenges succeed on process gaps, not on the merit of the decision.
simulation.conditions: Competitive public-sector procurement with formal challenge rights.
